intro.text: A noble house whose lord, Ashweather Cett, has made himself king of the Western Dominance after the Lord Ruler's fall.
A noble house of Scadrial, founded under the Final Empire, which takes the Western Dominance after the Lord Ruler's fall and is still a very powerful house centuries on.

description.text: House Cett counted for little across the empire as a whole, but in its own corner of the west no family was stronger, and few people elsewhere knew much of it.

Under the Lord Ruler, Ashweather did a great deal of business with Luthadel's nobles, but through lesser houses acting as fronts, so that he would not seem tied to the capital. The Ministry saw through it.
The house had existed for centuries before the Lord Ruler fell. A long history of skaa blood mixing into the family leaves it unable to produce Mistborn, and with only a few Mistings.

Like other high houses, it counts everyone it employs as members, though newcomers are treated as full members only once a generation or two has passed. In Elendel it holds parties in a lavishly decorated mansion of three storeys.
The Cetts have always been shrewd, calculating businesspeople, and they own several businesses, among them Ashweather Carriage and Coach.

items.text: After the Lord Ruler's death, House Cett seized the Western Dominance. Ashweather, newly crowned, shifted the seat of his rule from Tremredare to Fadrex City, which was smaller and easier to defend.

While Cett was taking the west, refugees fleeing rogue koloss flooded his lands. He tried to take on a nearby koloss garrison, which followed him for a time before suddenly turning on his army; he had to kill all five hundred and lost almost two thousand men.
The conquest was untidy. When it was done, his kingdom was a quilt of shaky alliances held together by the threat of invasion, and most of it rose against him once he marched away.
According to Hammond, the Allomancers who attacked Vin came from Ashweather Cett, who now styles himself King of the Western Dominance.

Cett brings a second army to Luthadel, soon after Straff Venture's. Breeze, who had been advising him and had let him believe the Lord Ruler's atium lay in the city, steered him there so the two armies would hold each other in check.
Cett's daughter, Allrianne, turns up at Elend's palace and throws her arms around Breeze. Dockson suggests holding her as leverage against her father.

Cett asks the Luthadel Assembly to make him king, promising rewards to those who back him. He is let into the city with a thousand soldiers and lodged in an empty keep, and his son Gneorndin invites Elend to talk.

Believing Cett ordered the attack on the candidates for king, Vin and Zane storm Keep Hasting, where he is staying, and kill or wound some three hundred men. They find Cett and his son, but leave the two of them alive.
Cett then pulls his army back from Luthadel.
Allrianne catches up with the army and urges her father to turn back to Luthadel instead of heading home.
When Allrianne rides into the fight alone, Cett's army joins Luthadel's defenders against Straff's forces. Afterwards Vin makes Cett, Penrod and Janarle accept Elend as their emperor.
While Ashweather was away, Aradan Yomen ousted House Cett and took over its kingdom.

Ashweather became the empire's foremost general. He directed most of the tactics in the siege of Fadrex City, the Cetts' old capital, and when koloss attacked, he took command of the army and led the city's defence.
The house holds a seat in the Elendel Senate, where its high lord speaks for everyone who works for the house or lives on its land. In 348 PC it is among the strongest factions in the government.

Allrianne founded House Ladrian with Breeze, while the Cett line carried on, with Westweather as heir by the early third century. In 348, Darlin Cett sits on Lady Steris's small council, urges a first strike, and flees the city once the bomb is confirmed.
